discipline: How people come to understand: a worked case before the abstraction, a story followed through time, "you are here", progressive disclosure, and what a reader can then DO (predict, diagnose, explain). AI-written; a design argument from reading the files, tested on no person.
verdict_on_present:
Right: plain names; one operational test per place; every mark settled against a Lean statement with its strength; unresolved items kept; line style for how far seen; it reported its own overlaps and hole. Keep all of that.

The picture is a fair second view for someone who already holds the idea. The data under it is dominated, and for a stranger's first ten minutes a node-link map is the wrong first view: no entry, no reading order, and 38 labelled arrows are 38 sentences to read. Ren's "yes" after five minutes is the read of the person who already has the schema; it does not tell us what a stranger gets.

The structure I propose contains the present one (same names, same decisions, same laws), so it cannot be worse on faithfulness or economy. Whether a stranger understands more is not settled by argument.
dominated_where: Free-text tests hide that places are combinations. 10 of the 15 tests or glosses contain an 'or' or a list. 'Past turning back' names two facts: the thing can no longer be kept (reading-a-loss-in-time exits 1, 2) and the rule is kept for good although read (readers-drawn-from-the-selected transition 2; loss-read-in-time-by-the-others transitions 1, 2). A stranger asks 'the fish or the quota?' and the map cannot answer.

'Arrow' mixes two things a reader takes as one ('this happens next'). 7 of the 38 arrows are two-way 'tipping in a parameter' between shaping-pays and shaping-costs: one line (does the return cover the cost) stated in seven models, drawn as traffic. The checkers say it: 'sides of a supplied parameter read in one cohort'. No law there shows a movement.
One law drawn twice: ClosedCapture.Thinned.kept_iff is both felt -> cost-counts (readers-drawn-from-the-selected exit 1) and felt -> past-turning-back (transition 2). It is one line with two sides.

28 of 88 items (16 'inside', 12 'unresolved') get no mark of their own; 14 of the inside/stays sit in holds-itself. Many are changes on a question the list never asks (which side is held, how fast the hold sets in). The two compose items of offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits are proved identities filed as 'unresolved'.

Overlap is found by remark, not computed: layout.json enters 'a case of' and 'with' for judged-inside by hand; felt/past-turning-back, noticers-gone/all-on-one, shaping-pays/holds-itself are in the checkers' notes only.

The hand layout carries a meaning nobody chose: sources left, three boxes with no arrow out on the right, 'The cost counts' top right, 'Past turning back' and 'Ended' below it. It reads as one good ending and two bad ones.
No case is data. The 15 examples come from 12 domains (the fishery appears in four), so nothing can be followed through time, and 'find a real case on it' means reading 15 tests.
Scale: 35 to 40 free tests, and family A's answers (past turning back, ended) are already in this region, so a flat list holds them twice or draws long arrows between regions.
proposal_in_one_paragraph: Make the primitive a short list of plain QUESTIONS one can ask of any case, each with two to four answers. The repository already has them: USES.md asks of any selection what it reads, what lies beyond, whether its rule can lock on what it picked, and who reads the loss and when. A PLACE is a named set of answers (the present names stay). A CHANGE is one question's answer changing, or the line between two answers, with its condition, strength and law. A REAL CASE is a path: the answers at each moment, and for each step the change that licenses it or "no law: supplied". A Lean witness is the same record: a case of one step. Two things are drawn: one case walked through time (the entry), and the board, where position is the answers and so is computed.
schema:
question: id; ask (a full plain sentence, en and zh, never a label on the page); of (what it is asked about: the rule, what is used up, those with a say); answers (ordered where there is an order; each: say in six words or fewer, and test = the Lean predicate or premise ids that make it true, e.g. RuleCapture.Locked); known_as (the field's own name for it).

place: id; name; answers (only the questions it fixes; the rest are open); example; how_far. Overlap and containment are computed from answers, never entered.

change: id; question; from; to; kind, one of four: moves (a course goes from one answer to another in time), line (which side of a threshold in a supplied quantity; nothing moves unless the quantity is changed from outside), stays (what keeps the answer), same-as (a proved identity between two models' questions); given (other questions' answers that must hold); when (plain, 20 words or fewer); strength; law; model (the dynamic); item (dynamic and exit or transition number); other_side (the companion of an iff); supplied (what the law takes as given and does not show); scope ("any question" for laws about every change).

case: id; name; standing (Lean witness / actual, tested / actual, read / illustration); steps (each: time, answers, by = a change id or "no law: supplied", evidence); bears (who bears what); web (link to its situations.json entry where one exists).

Unplaced items stay in a list with the reason.
drawn_from_it:
1. THE STRIP (first ten minutes). One case in five or six steps left to right. Each step is a card: the answers now, the one answer that changed, why in 20 words or fewer, line style for how far seen, and the other side of the fork greyed. A second case that forks the other way runs beneath it (one where the rule turned, one where it was kept). Each step links to its place. A step with no law says "supplied".

2. THE BOARD (the hour). The present boxes, placed by their answers. For this region: columns = who with a say can tell (no one / those who could are gone / only those ahead / someone not ahead); rows = can what is being lost still be kept (yes / no / ended); a band for where the rule comes from. A line change is drawn as a boundary between neighbouring cells with its law on it; a moves change as an arrow; a witness as a dot (one case seen here); a cell with no law is left visibly blank. A case's path is drawn over it as "you are here".

Not a third drawing: the question list printed is the sheet to fill for a real case, and each place's article is its record (lead, example, changes in, changes out, blank neighbours).

After ten minutes a stranger should retell the case, answer the questions for a case of their own, and say what decides the fork. After an hour: find their case's cell, list which changes out of it have a law and how strong, explain why noticing is not enough, and point to one blank.
worked_sample:
Six questions (shorthand in capitals is mine; the page prints the sentence).
RULE: where does the rule come from? from outside / rebuilt from its results, not settled / rebuilt, holding the side it picked / rebuilt, holding the other side.
USED: is something used up that the rule does not register? not said / yes / now registered.
WHO: who with a say can tell? no one / those who could are gone / only those ahead / someone not ahead.
KEPT: can what is being lost still be kept? yes / no / it has ended.
PAYS: does bending the rule pay those who do it? no / yes.
WAYS: how many ways are in use? several / one.

PLACES
- A rule set from outside = {RULE: from outside}
- Holds itself in place = {RULE: holding the side it picked}
- Drawing on what is not counted = {USED: yes}
- Judged only from inside = {RULE: holding picked, USED: yes, WHO: only those ahead}. Computed: inside the two above.
- Those who would notice are gone = {USED: yes, WHO: gone}
- Felt by someone with a say = {USED: yes, WHO: someone not ahead, KEPT: yes}
- Past turning back splits: {KEPT: no} (the thing), and {RULE: holding picked, WHO: someone not ahead}, kept for good (the rule).
- The cost counts splits: {USED: now registered, RULE: not settled} (ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss: stops favouring the winners past a limit), and {RULE: holding the other side, WHO: someone not ahead}.
- Ended = {KEPT: it has ended}

CHANGES (dynamic, item; how it is drawn now)
C1 moves RULE: not settled -> holding picked. Given: the rebuilt rule favours one side at every lead. Within two rebuildings; one is not enough. Sufficient; RuleCapture.uniform_locks, bound exact by Second.second_exact. capture-through-the-rule, transition 1. Now: 'inside', no arrow.
C2 line PAYS: no | yes, at "what comes back to the benders alone covers the cost". Exact; RuleShaping.favours_iff, disfavours_iff. shaping-the-rule-selected-by-what-comes-back, transition 1. The same line in six more models: that dynamic's transitions 2, 4, 5; shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected transition 2; offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits transitions 1, 2. Now: seven two-way arrows.
C3 same-as: givers paired with givers ARE the benders for PAYS. Proved identity; PairSelection.assorted_counts onto RuleShaping.favours_iff. offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits, compose 1 (and 2). Now: unresolved.
C4 moves WHO: no one -> someone not ahead. Given USED: yes, KEPT: yes. When the first moment anyone with a say can tell comes before the point of no return. Exact; Web.readableInTime_iff. reading-a-loss-in-time, transition 1. Now: uncounted -> felt.
C5 moves KEPT: yes -> no. Given USED: yes, WHO: no one, or only those being lost. Sufficient; Web.too_late_of_alike, too_late_of_own. reading-a-loss-in-time, exits 1, 2. Now: uncounted -> past-turning-back.
C6 line RULE, at the step the loss is read, given WHO: someone not ahead: winners at least as many as the others -> holding picked at every later step; fewer -> not held at the next step. Exact; ClosedCapture.Thinned.kept_iff. readers-drawn-from-the-selected, exit 1 and transition 2. Now: two arrows.
C7 moves RULE: holding picked -> holding the other side. Given WHO: someone not ahead, judged two steps running. Exact; ReadInTime.turned_iff, whose conclusion is Locked (reverse order) at every later step. loss-read-in-time-by-the-others, exit 1. Now: felt -> cost-counts.
C8 stays RULE: holding picked. Given WHO: someone not ahead who begins to count only after a number of rounds fixed by the starting numbers. Sufficient; ReadInTime.deadline. Same dynamic, transition 2. Now: felt -> past-turning-back.
C9 moves WHO: -> gone, given USED: yes. Witness; ReadingsSpread.Commons.cleared_spreads. readings-revised-spread-and-locked, exit 4. With it, stays RULE: holding, given they are removed before they register it. Sufficient; PoolFromCourse.window_never_read. the-lock-draws-its-readers-out, transition 1.
C10 moves KEPT: yes -> ended, given USED: yes: a dependant needs more than remains once the winners take all they can. Web.optimum_broken_iff_capacity (exact cut-off) joined by hand with optimum_ends_beyond (one-way). what-an-optimum-does-beyond-what-couples-in, transition 1.
C11 moves WHO: gone -> counted again. Sufficient; Becoming.not_allPersist_of_removes. selection-read-off-its-own-survivors, exit 1. Supplied from outside: the measure is taken over a fixed list of all who began.

A REAL CASE: situations.json's reward-model pipeline (standing: reading) is one step: {RULE: not rebuilt in the one pass written, USED: yes, WHO: raters cannot tell}. Its own summary reads no lock, so its path stops there, and the strip shows it stopping.
what_it_reveals:
Checked against the Lean signatures for uniform_locks, second_exact, turned_iff and both kept_iff; the rest is from the decisions' wording.

1. There is a law into the hold. Second.second_exact proves a course not Locked at step 1 and Locked at step 2; uniform_locks gives it from any start. The flat map reported "no law gives an arrow into the hold" because the place before the hold (rebuilt, not yet settled) was not on the list.

2. The exact way out of the hold leads into a hold. turned_iff concludes Locked (reverse order). "The cost counts" is drawn as a separate end, top right; by its own law it is the same condition on the other side, of which the same questions can be asked again. No law here says what the new hold leaves unregistered.

3. A cell with four laws and no name: someone not ahead can tell, and the hold is kept (C6's one side, C8, ReadInTime.kept_early_iff, kept_past_least). It is the precise content of "noticing is not enough", filed today under past-turning-back.

4. A loop among the questions, three legs of different standing: USED: yes moves WHO to gone (one witness, two readings); WHO: gone keeps RULE holding (sufficient: window_never_read; necessary: locked_along); RULE holding lets the loss grow, which is supplied (Accrues is a hypothesis of the laws). Every law that moves WHO toward "someone not ahead" takes something from outside the loop as given: a fixed list (C11), a fixed date (PoolCourse.scheduled_apart, witness), a pool that already holds the dependant (Clearing.pool_closes_gap, witness). unselected-beyond-the-coupling-closure exit 7 and compose 1 read that nothing inside secures a noticer. On the flat map these are five separate arrows uncounted -> felt.

5. Holes by count: no change into USED: yes (it is given in every law), none into "only those ahead" (judged-inside has no arrow in), none out of the three right-hand boxes.
loses_or_risks:
- The immediate picture. Named boxes are what Ren recognised; a board can look like a form or a taxonomy. Keep the names in the cells and lead with the case.
- A product of answers has cells no law covers. Draw only cells with a law or a case; keep "blank: nothing shown" apart from "shown not to occur".
- Choosing questions claims more than choosing places: that the conditions factor. They do not fully (the record of shaping-read-by-readers-drawn-from-the-selected says the lock and the capacity to shape it are one loop). A wrong factoring misleads more evenly than a wrong box. 'given' and 'same-as' carry the dependence; items that will not fit stay listed.
- A story persuades beyond its weakest join. The laws in one strip are proved on different models; WHOLE-PICTURE counts ten joins in the capture chain, six proved. Each step must show its join's standing.
- The question labels could become new private words. Print the sentence, not the label.
- It does not shorten the prose by itself.
- I read families A and E, and D by names only. The count of questions for the whole atlas (my guess: 10 to 14) is a guess.
cost_to_build:
By script from what exists: each change's law, strength, model and item (dynamics.json exits and transitions); 'supplied' from each exit's 'drops' against premises.json; pairing the two sides of an iff and finding one law cited by several items (8 such laws in this region); kind 'line' for 'tipping in a parameter', 'exact threshold' and 'critical mass'; overlap and containment; blank cells; the loop among questions; board positions; the sheet; article skeletons. A grep can check that a change's law mentions the Lean predicate of its 'to' answer.

By reading: the questions and their answers (the real design work; six here); each place's answers (15 small judgments); for each of the 88 decisions, which question and whether it moves in time or is a line (needs the statement: is there a course, or a supplied parameter?). Where 'from' and 'to' differ on two questions, the item is flagged; that flag is how the two split places above were found. The cases' steps are written by hand and checked. For this region that is one more adjudication round, smaller than the first because the decisions carry over.
scales_to_other_families:
A (Absorption and ending): holds, and better than a flat list. A is mostly one question, KEPT, with answers yes / at a juncture / no / ended, plus "deferred by a reserve". This region already uses two of them. Its 25 transitions are 11 windows or deadlines, 6 exact thresholds and 3 tippings: lines and time bounds on that question in different models (margin-of-a-regime exit 1, RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below: it ends exactly where the start is below H + y). Where it strains: about five dynamics (attraction-is-not-returning, basins-of-a-determined-law, every-loss-passes-a-juncture, what-a-gate-keeps, not-going-out-of-a-region) are about every question at once (Run.leaving_needs: leaving a region needs a move that does not keep it). They have no cell; they are the legend, what "stays" and "no return" mean. Without scope: "any question" the structure breaks there. three-outcomes-of-a-loss exit 3 (Crossing.loss_does_not_decide) is a three-way fork nothing decides: a change with no line, which the schema allows.

E (Waiting and reciprocity): holds with one new question, "who is giving?" (all / some withheld / none), asked of each member. Its laws are lines in tolerance, window and chain length (Tolerance.restores_iff, exact; thin_absorbed; PairChance.burst_absorbs). Its selection half is not new: offspring-read-from-giving-that-waits and what-decides-giving-against-keeping-on-a-flow transition 1 (PairFlow.Routes.gap_iff) are the PAYS line again, through same-as. Where it strains: the conditions are about the shape of a network (chains of waits), which a board cannot show; the case's web must carry it.

Whole atlas, counted: of 321 exits 160 are witnesses; of 103 transitions 74 are exact thresholds, tippings or windows. Movements in time are the minority of what remains, so an arrows-first map will keep filing most items "inside". A witness becomes a dot: a case of one step.
false_premise:
Three.

1. "Optimal" and "Pareto frontier" cannot be shown by design. One can show that a given structure is dominated, as here. Whether a stranger understands more in five minutes is settled only by two or three people reading: say it back, place a case, say what happens next. The counts also trade against each other (five minutes against an hour, few words against visible limits), so there is a frontier with several points, not one best.

2. "The data structure that projects onto the map" takes the map as the thing to get right. For understanding, the first view is a case followed through time; the map is what a reader can use after that.

3. Not dualistic is not reached by neutral names alone. The layout already says good ending and bad endings. And the map need not pretend no one bears anything: who bears what is said per case, plainly, apart from the place names.
first_change:
Add the case as a record: a path of steps, each giving the answers to the five questions USES.md already asks and the decision that licenses the step, or "no law: supplied". Draw one case, the fishery (marked as an illustration), walked across the present map, with the reward-model pipeline beside it stopping after one step.

It needs no re-adjudication, gives a stranger an entry and a reading order, can be put before a person the same day, and forces the rest: each step must say which answer changed, and where the case cannot step ("past turning back: the fish or the rule?") the place list shows where it must split.
